changed: separated the validated public HTTPS browser origin from the listening address and local authenticated CLI endpoint while preserving existing direct LAN and loopback behavior
required header-authenticated dashboard event streams and enforced the configured browser Origin without trusting Host or forwarding headers
documented a supported Caddy reverse-proxy recipe for private-CA LAN and public-domain certificates, including upgrade, certificate replacement, recovery and rollback
added a pinned real-TLS Caddy fixture and CI coverage for pairing, API access, SSE, browser access, local CLI fallback, certificate failures, backend failure and plaintext downgrade prevention
summary: The controller now supports an explicitly configured HTTPS public origin through a loopback-only Caddy backend while local CLI access remains independent of public DNS, proxy and certificate availability.
Permanent pairing credentials are no longer sent in SSE query strings, browser transport checks use configured origins, and proxy mode does not trust forwarded headers or expose MCP publicly.
The supported deployment documentation covers private-CA LAN and public-domain certificate workflows without changing firewall rules, system trust, the installed controller or native Node TLS.
